title: Rounding of the Courtesy Credit on Savings Accounts by Deposit History
content:
How the courtesy credit on an account of Savings & Money Market Accounts is rounded follows the deposit history of the account: the count of deposits posted to it in the twelve calendar months ending on the review date.

Where 4 or more deposits posted in that window, the courtesy credit is rounded half up to the whole dollar. Where 2 or 3 deposits posted in that window, it is truncated to the dime. Where fewer than 2 deposits posted in that window, it is rounded half up to the cent.

### The same figure under each rule

Take a hypothetical courtesy credit, before rounding, of 13.6750 USD. Under the first rule it becomes 14.00 USD, since 0.6750 stands above the half dollar. Under the second it becomes 13.60 USD, truncation discarding what lies below the dime rather than rounding it up. Under the third it becomes 13.68 USD.

A second hypothetical figure of 4.5000 USD becomes 5.00 USD under the first rule, 4.50 USD under the second and 4.50 USD under the third, which shows that the three rules do not always part company.

### Boundary of the counts

A count of exactly 4 deposits falls under the first rule, a count of exactly 2 under the second, and a count of 1 or 0 under the third.
